function: Beam control: predicts future UAV pointing angles, then selects TX/RX activation patterns (255 beams) of a row-selective patch array for THz UAV-to-UAV links (pp. 7-9)
system: UAV-to-UAV THz link at 272.5 GHz; 8x8 row-selective microstrip patch arrays (255 activation patterns) at TX and RX; LoS channel, no RIS (pp. 3, 6)
method: Two-stage causal Transformer (Conv1D, RoPE; 4 and 5 layers, d=256) with codebook cross-attention; supervised training with Wrapped Cauchy, focal and distillation losses from exhaustive-search oracle (pp. 7-10)
data_channel: Own dataset: 10,000 samples, 200 scenarios, five UAV profiles (one from measured accelerations); simulated LoS THz channel (free-space, ITU-R P.676 absorption); HFSS patterns (pp. 2, 6, 11)
test_conditions: Training and testing on the same five mobility profiles (split not stated); out-of-distribution maneuvers left as future work; no other antenna or band tested (pp. 11-12)
baselines: Non-learned: ARSA exhaustive search (upper bound), fixed and adaptive 3D sectored antennas; learned: UCB bandit pattern selection over 36 patterns [40] (pp. 11-12)
metrics: Angular MAE and 3D angular error, antenna gain and achievable capacity over time, capacity efficiency versus exhaustive search, R2 score, beam-match accuracy, inference latency (pp. 12-17)
complexity: Order O(d_m^2 (LT+N_b)), about 3.6e7 operations, versus ARSA 6.5e4 operations and O(N_b^2); latency 0.36 ms on Tesla T4, ARSA over 1 s (pp. 16-17)
openness: Code, UAV trajectory dataset and antenna radiation patterns released at https://github.com/Miladbaf/CORTEX (p. 18)
q1_support: p. 6: "modeled as the product of the free-space spreading coefficient hs and the absorption coefficient ha"; custom analytic LoS THz channel from [30], with ITU-R P.676 used only for absorption; no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured channel.
q2_support: p. 12: "outside the training distribution, Stage I accuracy may degrade"; the same five profiles serve for training and testing, and out-of-distribution adaptation is declared outside the scope of the work.
q3_support: p. 12: "applies UCB learning to select from the curated 36 pattern space using instantaneous gain as reward"; p. 11: "performs exhaustive search across all 255 radiation patterns"; capacity and gain compared in Figs. 7-11.
q4_support: p. 17: "CORTEX achieves an inference latency of 0.36 ms on a Tesla T4 GPU"; p. 16: order O(d_m^2 (LT+N_b)) and about 3.6e7 operations (Table 10).
q5_support: p. 18: "The UAV trajectory dataset, the antenna radiation patterns, and the source codes are available at" https://github.com/Miladbaf/CORTEX.
notes: Included as area 6, which wins over area 3: learned beam control of UAV-to-UAV THz links, framed by the paper as 6G non-terrestrial networks (p. 1). ris=0: the array is a reconfigurable antenna, not a RIS. q1=0 because the channel is a custom LoS model [30] and ITU-R P.676 only gives the absorption term (reviewer may confirm); one of five UAV profiles derives from measured accelerations [20], but the channel is simulated. q3=1 relies on UCB [40], a bandit learner over 36 patterns, as the learned baseline; no deep-learning baseline is compared. q2=0: evaluation is in-distribution and the split is not stated.
